name: Hvar Town Old Town and Harbour
tagline: The marble-square heart of it all
description: The historic, car-free core around St Stephen's Square, the cathedral and the yacht-lined harbour. This is Hvar at its most lively and glamorous, with cafes, restaurants, bars and the summer buzz all within a short walk of the waterfront and the ferry quay.
bestFor: First-time visitors who want to be in the middle of everything
pros: Best dining and nightlife on hand
cons: Most expensive and most crowded in summer
Noise from bars can carry late

name: Fortica Hillside and Residential Lanes
description: The stepped lanes climbing above the old town toward the Fortica fortress, mixing residential homes and small guesthouses. You trade waterfront convenience for calm, greenery and panoramic views over the harbour and the Pakleni Islands, while staying a short, if uphill, walk from the square.
bestFor: Nomads wanting quiet and views close to the center
pros: Peaceful away from the harbour crowds
cons: Steep steps and climbs to reach it

name: Stari Grad
tagline: The calmer, older port across the island
description: Croatia's oldest town and the island's main car-ferry port, sitting in a sheltered bay. Stari Grad is quieter, more local and more affordable than Hvar Town, with an ancient old core, the UNESCO-listed Stari Grad Plain nearby, and an easygoing, lived-in Dalmatian pace.
bestFor: Longer, calmer stays and better value
pros: Quieter and cheaper than Hvar Town
cons: A drive or bus from Hvar Town

name: Jelsa
description: A pretty, tree-shaded harbour town on the island's north coast, surrounded by pine, vineyards and swimming coves. Jelsa is more residential and family-friendly than Hvar Town, offering a slower, authentic island base with cafes, a small marina and easy access to beaches and wine country.
bestFor: Slow living, families and nature-focused stays
